sources.citation: Ubels, Edward H. 1983. Mood and aspect in Karang. Studies in African Linguistics 14(1): 47-70. DOI 10.32473/sal.v14i1.107535
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Section 1.1 'Phonology and morphology of the verb' (p. 49) and fn. 2 describe tone only: every verb root carries one tone, two tone classes (mid, low), orthography marks high/low/rising with mid unmarked; the words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the article. Refers the compiler to Ubels & Ubels 1980 for the phonology.

sources.note: Not Karang but the closest published phonology-grammar of a sister language (Mbum, mbum1254); Ubels 1983 names it as the only related language with published phonological information. Useful only as a related-variety comparison, not as a Karang statement.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Karang language' (citing Ethnologue 18th ed. 2015; Binam Bikoi ed. 2012 ALCAM)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; notes the orthography marks high tone with an acute accent; dialects Karang and Ngumi; related varieties Sakpu, Nzakmbay, Mbere.

sources.quote: ke 1 kè prép 1) avec 2) de (endroit) 3) à (temp) … ke 2 kē pron il … ké 1 ké prép à; dans; de … ké 2 ké pron il ké gi Qu'il vienne. … kay 1 káy n saison sèche … kay 2 kày n ver; chenille; microbe … bah 1 báá n père … bah 2 bāā v chercher … naŋ 1 nàŋ n mil … naŋ 2 nāŋ v écraser
sources.note: No prose statement was readable (the introduction/alphabet pages of webonary.org/karang are IP-blocked here and the the Internet Archive copies were deferred), but the dictionary itself gives every entry an etic phonetic form with tone marked on each vowel at three heights (acute high, macron mid, grave low; occasional caron rising), and its numbered homographs include exact tonal minimal sets on identical segments, e.g. ke [kè] 'avec' / ke [kē] 'il' / ké [ké] 'à, dans' and subjunctive 'il', kay [káy] 'saison sèche' / [kày] 'ver', bah [báá] 'père' / [bāā] 'chercher', naŋ [nàŋ] 'mil' / [nāŋ] '…

sources.note: Secondhand, one passage in a pan-African survey of tone orthographies (seen only as a search-engine extract of the text, not opened): in Karang, an Adamawa language of Cameroon, just the first syllable of each word is tone-marked while later syllables are systematically unmarked (citing Ubels & Ubels 1986). Whether Bird also states that non-initial tone is non-contrastive was NOT verified; number of tones not given in what was seen. The cited 'Ubels & Ubels 1986' source itself was not identified (possibly the 1986 Alfabe karaŋ or an orthography statement; not the 1980 phonology by date).
